brief:
Western nations' targeted sanctions against Israeli settlers prove insufficient to prevent their expansion, Al Jazeera English reported. A recent settler takeover in Jericho has exposed the limitations of restrictions focused narrowly on individual settlers and their organizations rather than addressing the broader Israeli state apparatus.

The case demonstrates how sanctions designed to isolate settlers from financial systems and markets may inadvertently shield the Israeli government from accountability. Without measures targeting state institutions themselves, critics argue, such sanctions allow the state to distance itself from settler actions while maintaining the conditions that enable them.
dek: The settler takeover in Jericho exposes the inadequacy of sanctions targeting only settlers and their organisations.
title: Western sanctions on settlers fail to curb Israeli takeover in Jericho
